title: Chapter 19. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — III: the childhood pastimes of Nimai
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 19: padas on the Lord's childhood from the "Balya-lila" section of the GPT (2.2). First come three padas which Narahari Chakravarti quotes in the Bhakti-ratnakara while showing the house of Jagannatha Mishra (the first feeding with rice, Nimai in His father's arms, the first steps); then a large cycle in which the old men and elderly women of Navadvipa, coming at dawn to the house of Shachi, gaze at Gaura, bless Him and recall His childhood pranks. Almost the whole of this cycle is found in the Gaura-charita-chintamani of Narahari Chakravarti (chapters 5 and 6 of the "morning pastimes": the love of the old men and the love of the women in vatsalya) — a strong argument for Chakravarti; two padas (nos. 24 and 27) have not been found in any witness. The index of poets of GPT2 assigns the padas of the section to Chakravarti (those found in the BR) or to an undistinguished "Narahari Dasa" (the GCC padas); none to Sarakara. According to Majumdar, the padas on the birth and childhood of Nimai are late: Narahari Sarakara, who lived in Shrikhanda, did not see the Lord's childhood, and the "Narahari" padas known only from the GPT are unreliable for attribution. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 2.1–2.2 were checked throughout in GPT1 (tesseract recognition): the catalogue had missed 14 padas of this section (13 of them in this chapter). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. The childhood games of the Lord are the lila of Bhagavan, not an ordinary childhood (note 2). The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "nadīyāra nārī puruṣa…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 10; BR)

The first feeding with rice: the men and women of Nadia gather with gifts; the Child sits on Nilambara's lap in new ornaments; tasting grains of sweet rice, He smiles; all praise Shachi and Jagannatha. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); tripadi with chains of chiming sounds.1

নদীয়ার নারী পুরুষ, সুকৃতি মানি, মনে মহা আনন্দিত হৈয়া ।
নিমাইর অন্নপ্রাশনে, সকলে আইসেন, নানা সামগ্রী লৈঞা ॥

nadīyāra nārī puruṣa, sukṛti māni, mane mahā ānandita haiyā |
nimāira annaprāśane, sakale āisena, nānā sāmagrī laiñā ||

nadīyāra nārī puruṣa — the women and men of Nadia; sukṛti māni — deeming [it] the fruit of pious deeds; mane mahā ānandita haiyā — greatly rejoicing at heart; nimāira anna-prāśane — at Nimai's first feeding with rice; sakale āisena — all come; nānā sāmagrī laiñā — bringing various gifts

1.1The men and women of Nadia, counting it the reward of their pious deeds, in great joy
gather for Nimai's first feeding with rice — each bringing various gifts.2

শচীসুতশোভা, দেখে আঁখি ভরি, নীলাম্বর ভাগ্যমন্তের কোলে ।
নব নব আভরণময়, কটীতটে পট্টধটী, অঞ্চল দোলে ॥

śacīsutaśobhā, dekhe ām̐khi bhari, nīlāmbara bhāgyamantera kole |
naba naba ābharaṇamaya, kaṭītaṭe paṭṭadhaṭī, añcala dole ||

śacī-suta-śobhā — the beauty of Shachi's son; dekhe ām̐khi bhari — they see to their eyes' fill; nīlāmbara bhāgyamantera kole — on the lap of fortunate Nilambara; naba naba ābharaṇa-maya — all in ever-new ornaments; kaṭī-taṭe paṭṭa-dhaṭī — a silk cloth on the hips; añcala dole — the hem sways

1.2They gaze their fill at the beauty of Shachi's son on the lap of fortunate Nilambara:3 all in ever-new ornaments, a silk cloth about His hips, the hem of His garment swaying.

হেমসরসীজ জিনি তনুখানি, মুখে কি উপমা চাঁদের ঘটা ।
মিষ্ট-অন্নকণিকা, গ্রহণে কিবা অদ্ভুত, মৃদু হাসির ছটা ॥

hemasarasīja jini tanukhāni, mukhe ki upamā cām̐dera ghaṭā |
miṣṭa-annakaṇikā, grahaṇe kibā adbhuta, mṛdu hāsira chaṭā ||

hema-sarasīja jini — surpassing a golden lotus; tanukhāni — the body; mukhe ki upamā — what comparison for the face; cām̐dera ghaṭā — the splendour of the moon; miṣṭa-anna-kaṇikā grahaṇe — on taking grains of sweet rice; kibā adbhuta — how wondrous; mṛdu hāsira chaṭā — the flash of a gentle smile

1.3His body surpasses a golden lotus, and His face — what can compare? — the splendour of the moon; how wondrously, tasting grains of sweet rice, He flashes a gentle smile!

এহেন উৎসবে, কেবা ধরে ধৃতি, কহিতে কৌতুক না আইসে মুখে ।
সবে শচী জগন্নাথে প্রশংসয়ে, নরহরি হিয়া উথলে সুখে ॥

ehena utsabe, kebā dhare dhṛti, kahite kautuka nā āise mukhe |
sabe śacī jagannāthe praśaṃsaye, narahari hiyā uthale sukhe ||

ehena utsabe — at such a festival; kebā dhare dhṛti — who keeps composure; kahite kautuka nā āise mukhe — the joy does not come to the mouth to be told; sabe — all; śacī jagannāthe praśaṃsaye — praise Shachi and Jagannatha; narahari hiyā uthale sukhe — Narahari's heart overflows with happiness

1.4At such a festival who can keep his composure? The joy cannot be put into words.
All praise Shachi and Jagannatha — Narahari's heart overflows with happiness.

catalogue did not know it (new row NG-262). BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, p. 768; ed. 1960, vv. 956–959): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha Mishra, says that here at six months the Lord was given His first rice and named, and quotes the pada. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first feeding with rice (annaprashana) — CB Adi 4; CC Adi 14; Murari 1.6. as an infant and a child for the sake of His eternal associates who love Him in vatsalya (parental love). Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra are His eternal parents (in Krishna-lila, Yashoda and Nanda, CC Adi 13); their love, like the love of the people of Navadvipa, is pure prema, not worldly attachment. So the whole Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) understands Gaura's childhood games, and so they are to be understood in all the padas of this chapter.

2. Narahari — "jagannātha miśra mahāsukhe…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 11; BR)

Jagannatha Mishra fondles his son; Nimai climbs down from his lap and crawls about the courtyard, looking back; Shachi calls Him into her arms — "dust will stick to You"; He climbs up to her, smiling. Raga tudi. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).4

জগন্নাথ মিশ্র মহাসুখে ।
পুত্র কোলে করি চুম্ব দেয় চাঁদমুখে ॥

jagannātha miśra mahāsukhe |
putra kole kari cumba deya cām̐damukhe ||

jagannātha miśra mahā-sukhe — Jagannatha Mishra in great happiness; putra kole kari — taking his son on his lap; cumba deya cām̐da-mukhe — kisses the moonlike face

2.1Jagannatha Mishra in great happiness
takes his son on his lap and kisses the moonlike face.

শিরে কেশভূষণ সাজায় ।
আগুলি চালিতে স্নেহ উথলে হিয়ায় ॥

śire keśabhūṣaṇa sājāya |
āguli cālite sneha uthale hiyāya ||

śire keśa-bhūṣaṇa sājāya — adorns the hair on His head; āguli cālite — running his fingers [through it]; sneha uthale hiyāya — love overflows in his heart

2.2The father adorns the hair on His little head —
running his fingers through it, his heart overflows with love.

নিমাই বাপের কোল হৈতে ।
ভঙ্গী করি নাময়ে অঙ্গনে বেড়াইতে ॥

nimāi bāpera kola haite |
bhaṅgī kari nāmaye aṅgane beṛāite ||

nimāi bāpera kola haite — Nimai from His father's lap; bhaṅgī kari — gracefully; nāmaye — climbs down; aṅgane beṛāite — to roam about the courtyard

2.3From His father's lap Nimai
gracefully gets down to roam about the courtyard.

হামাগুড়ি বেড়ায় অঙ্গনে ।
সোণার নূপুর বাজে সুচারু চরণে ॥

hāmāguṛi beṛāya aṅgane |
soṇāra nūpura bāje sucāru caraṇe ||

hāmāguṛi beṛāya aṅgane — crawls on all fours about the courtyard; soṇāra nūpura bāje — golden nupuras ring; sucāru caraṇe — on the lovely feet

2.4On all fours He crawls about the courtyard;
golden nupuras ring on His lovely feet.5

চলিতে হেরই উলটিয়া ।
চলনমাধুরী মিশ্র দেখে দাঁড়াইয়া ॥

calite herai ulaṭiyā |
calanamādhurī miśra dekhe dām̐ṛāiyā ||

calite — while moving; heraï ulaṭiyā — looks back; calana-mādhurī — the sweetness of His movement; miśra dekhe dām̐ṛāiyā — Mishra stands and watches

2.5As He crawls, He looks back;
Mishra stands watching the sweetness of His movements.

সমুখে আসিয়া কহে মায় ।
কোলে চড়সিয়া বাপ ধূলি লাগে গায় ॥

samukhe āsiyā kahe māya |
kole caṛasiyā bāpa dhūli lāge gāya ||

samukhe āsiyā — coming before [Him]; kahe māya — the mother says; kole caṛasiyā — come up onto my lap; bāpa — darling (lit. "father", an endearment); dhūli lāge gāya — dust sticks to the body

2.6His mother comes before Him and says:
"Come up into my arms, darling — dust is sticking to Your body."

জননীর হাতে হাত দিয়া ।
কোলে উঠে লহু লহু হাসিয়া হাসিয়া ॥

jananīra hāte hāta diyā |
kole uṭhe lahu lahu hāsiyā hāsiyā ||

jananīra hāte hāta diyā — putting His hand in His mother's hand; kole uṭhe — climbs onto her lap; lahu lahu — slowly; hāsiyā hāsiyā — smiling and smiling

2.7Putting His little hand in His mother's hand,
He climbs onto her lap, smiling and smiling.

দুগ্ধবিন্দু সম দন্তজ্যোতি ।
হাসিতে প্রকাশ তায় কেবা ধরে ধৃতি ॥

dugdhabindu sama dantajyoti |
hāsite prakāśa tāya kebā dhare dhṛti ||

dugdha-bindu sama — like drops of milk; danta-jyoti — the shine of His teeth; hāsite prakāśa tāya — when it shows in His smile; kebā dhare dhṛti — who keeps composure

2.8His little teeth shine like drops of milk;
when they show in His smile — who can keep his composure?

দুটী আঁখে যার পানে চায় ।
তারে নিরন্তর সুখ-সমুদ্রে ভাসায় ॥

duṭī ām̐khe yāra pāne cāya |
tāre nirantara sukha-samudre bhāsāya ||

duṭī ām̐khe — with both eyes; yāra pāne cāya — at whom He looks; tāre — him; nirantara — ceaselessly; sukha-samudre bhāsāya — makes float in an ocean of happiness

2.9Whomever He looks at with both eyes,
him He immerses for ever in an ocean of happiness.

জননীর কোলে ভাল শোহে ।
নরহরি নিছনি ভুবন-মন-মোহে ॥

jananīra kole bhāla śohe |
narahari nichani bhubana-mana-mohe ||

jananīra kole — on His mother's lap; bhāla śohe — shines beautifully; narahari nichani — Narahari offers himself (the nichhani rite); bhubana-mana-mohe — to the Enchanter of the world's heart

2.10Beautifully He shines on His mother's lap;
Narahari offers himself to the Enchanter of the world's heart.6

ed. 1960, vv. 970–979): Ishana shows the courtyard where the Lord crawled on His knees (jānu-caṃkramaṇa), quotes the pada of Vasu Ghosha "ek mukhe ki kahiba" (GPT no. 2, chapter 12) and after it this one. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Cf. Murari 1.6; CC Adi 14. (cf. chapter 17, note 34). The signature of this cycle is usually "Narahari offers himself…" or "Narahari's life is Nimai".

3. Narahari — "śacī ṭhākurāṇī cāru chām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 65, no. 12; BR)

The first steps: Shachi teaches Gora to walk, holding out her finger; He stands up, takes two or four steps, lets go of the finger and falls; His mother takes Him in her arms and nurses Him. Raga tudi. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).7

শচী ঠাকুরাণী চারু ছাঁদে ।
হাটন শিখায় গোরাচাঁদে ॥

śacī ṭhākurāṇī cāru chām̐de |
hāṭana śikhāya gorācām̐de ||

śacī ṭhākurāṇī — Shachi Thakurani; cāru chām̐de — in a lovely way, tenderly; hāṭana śikhāya — teaches walking; gorācām̐de — Gorachand

3.1Shachi Thakurani tenderly
teaches Gorachand to walk.

মৃদু মৃদু কহেন হাসিয়া ।
ধর মোর অঙ্গুলি আসিয়া ॥

mṛdu mṛdu kahena hāsiyā |
dhara mora aṅguli āsiyā ||

mṛdu mṛdu kahena hāsiyā — very gently she says, smiling; dhara mora aṅguli āsiyā — come and take hold of my finger

3.2Very gently she says, smiling:
"Come, take hold of my finger."

শুনি সুখে নদীয়ার শশী ।
মায়ের অঙ্গুলি ধরে হাসি ॥

śuni sukhe nadīyāra śaśī |
māyera aṅguli dhare hāsi ||

śuni — hearing; sukhe — joyfully; nadīyāra śaśī — the Moon of Nadia; māyera aṅguli dhare — takes hold of His mother's finger; hāsi — smiling

3.3Hearing this, the Moon of Nadia joyfully
takes hold of His mother's finger with a smile.

ধীরে ধীরে উঠিয়া দাঁড়ায় ।
দুই চারি পদ চলি যায় ॥

dhīre dhīre uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya |
dui cāri pada cali yāya ||

dhīre dhīre — slowly, slowly; uṭhiyā dām̐ṛāya — rises and stands; dui cāri pada — two or four steps; cali yāya — He walks

3.4Slowly, slowly He rises and stands up,
and takes two or four steps.

ছাড়িয়া অঙ্গুলি পড়ে ভূমে ।
শচী কোলে লৈঞা মুখ চুমে ॥

chāṛiyā aṅguli paṛe bhūme |
śacī kole laiñā mukha cume ||

chāṛiyā aṅguli — letting go of the finger; paṛe bhūme — falls to the ground; śacī kole laiñā — Shachi, taking Him on her lap; mukha cume — kisses His face

3.5Letting go of the finger, He falls to the ground;
Shachi takes Him in her arms and kisses His little face.

কোলে চড়ি চরণ দোলায় ।
বাজয়ে নূপুর রাঙ্গা পায় ॥

kole caṛi caraṇa dolāya |
bājaye nūpura rāṅgā pāya ||

kole caṛi — climbing onto her lap; caraṇa dolāya — swings His feet; bājaye nūpura — the nupuras ring; rāṅgā pāya — on the reddish feet

3.6Climbing onto her lap, He swings His little feet,
and the nupuras ring on His reddish soles.

আঙ্গুলে কচালি স্তন পীয়ে ।
নাহি যে উপমা তায় দিয়ে ॥

āṅgule kacāli stana pīye |
nāhi ye upamā tāya diye ||

āṅgule kacāli — fingering with His little fingers; stana pīye — drinks at the breast; nāhi ye upamā — there is no comparison; tāya diye — to give for it

3.7Fingering with His little hand, He drinks at the breast —
there is no comparison for it.

চারিদিকে চাহে ভঙ্গী করি ।
তাহাতে নিছনি নরহরি ॥

cāridike cāhe bhaṅgī kari |
tāhāte nichani narahari ||

cāridike cāhe — looks about on all sides; bhaṅgī kari — with charming gestures; tāhāte — for that; nichani narahari — Narahari offers himself

3.8He looks about on all sides with charming gestures —
Narahari offers himself for this.

wave (ed. 1912, pp. 770–771; ed. 1960, vv. 990–997, "todi"): Ishana says that here in the courtyard the Lord took His first steps, quotes a verse from Murari's Shri-Krishna-Chaitanya-carita (part 1: "walking with His reddish feet, He took from the earth the fever of separation") and the pada. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The first steps — Murari 1.6; CB Adi 4; cf. the pada of Vasu Ghosha "māyera aṅguli dhari" (chapter 12).

4. Narahari — "gaura-badana sukha-sadana sudhāmaya…" (GPT1 p. 66, no. 15; GCC)

The old men of Navadvipa gaze at Gaura's face: each offers himself for Him; trembling, in tears, leaning on one another, they say: who created Mishra's son, who has stolen our hearing, mind and eyes? A moment without Him is like a kalpa; people tease us as madmen, we have forgotten all order in eating and sleeping, home has grown hateful, we have no love for our own sons. Yatharaga. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in his Gaura-charita-chintamani; Vrajabuli with chains of chiming sounds.8

গৌরবদন সুখসদন সুধাময় ঘন ঘন বৃদ্ধ পুরুষগণ হেরি ।
কত কত জনম সফল মানি নিজ নিজ তনু তনু নিছনি করত কত বেরি ॥

gaurabadana sukhasadana sudhāmaya ghana ghana bṛddha puruṣagaṇa heri |
kata kata janama saphala māni nija nija tanu tanu nichani karata kata beri ||

gaura-badana — Gaura's face; sukha-sadana — abode of happiness; sudhāmaya — full of nectar; ghana ghana — again and again; bṛddha puruṣa-gaṇa heri — the old men, gazing; kata kata janama saphala māni — deeming many births fruitful; nija nija tanu tanu nichani karata — each offers his whole body for Him; kata beri — many times

4.1Again and again the old men gaze at the face of Gaura — the abode of happiness, full of nectar; counting many of their births crowned with fruit, each again and again offers his whole self for Him.

টলমল করু নয়নে জল ছল ছল বিপুল পুলক কুলে মণ্ডিত গাত ।
কাহুক করে কর করি অবলম্বন কোই কহত মৃদু মধুরিম বাত ॥

ṭalamala karu nayane jala chala chala bipula pulaka kule maṇḍita gāta |
kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana koi kahata mṛdu madhurima bāta ||

ṭalamala karu — they totter; nayane jala chala chala — tears brim in the eyes; bipula pulaka kule maṇḍita gāta — the body adorned with abundant thrills; kāhuka kare kara kari abalambana — leaning on another's hand; koi kahata — someone says; mṛdu madhurima bāta — soft, sweet words

4.2They totter, their eyes brimming with tears, their bodies covered with abundant thrills; leaning on another's hand, someone speaks soft, sweet words:

মিশ্রতনয়ে কহ কো নিরমায়ল হরণ শ্রবণ মন লোচন মোর ।
পলক না হেরি কল্প সম লাগত অথির করই ধৃতি রহই ন থোর ॥

miśratanaye kaha ko niramāyala haraṇa śrabaṇa mana locana mora |
palaka nā heri kalpa sama lāgata athira karai dhṛti rahai na thora ||

miśra-tanaye — Mishra's son; kaha — tell; ko niramāyala — who fashioned; haraṇa śrabaṇa mana locana mora — who has stolen my hearing, mind and eyes; palaka nā heri — not seeing for a moment; kalpa sama lāgata — it seems like a kalpa; athira karaï — it unsettles [me]; dhṛti rahaï na thora — not a little steadiness remains

4.3"Tell me, who fashioned Mishra's son, who has stolen my hearing, my mind and my eyes? A moment when I do not see Him is like a kalpa; I am thrown into turmoil, and not a drop of steadiness remains.9

Gaura's welfare — this is how vatsalya, parental love, shows itself: in it the devotee forgets the Lord's majesty and, seeing Him as in need of protection, entreats all the gods on His behalf (cf. the cowherds of Vraja and Yashoda entrusting Krishna to the protection of the gods, Bhag. 10.6, 10.7). āṅgināra mājhe priya parikara beṣṭita basiyā gorā |
sundara-badanacām̐da jhalakaye gākhāni soṇāra pārā ||

āṅginār mājhe — in the middle of the courtyard; priya parikara beṣṭita — surrounded by dear associates; basiyā gorā — Gora sits; sundara-badana-cām̐da jhalakaye — the beautiful moonlike face flashes; gākhāni soṇāra pārā — the body like gold

naba naba saba ki kaba mālyāni se śobhā-sāyare bhāse |

15. Narahari — "rajanī-prabhāte śacīdebī cite…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 26; GCC)

Yatharaga. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC.28

রজনীপ্রভাতে শচীদেবী চিতে আনন্দের নাহি ওর ।
ও মুখ নিরখি নারে সম্বরিতে নয়ানে বহয়ে লোর ॥

rajanīprabhāte śacīdebī cite ānandera nāhi ora |
o mukha nirakhi nāre sambarite nayāne bahaye lora ||

rajanī-prabhāte — at dawn; śacīdebī cite — in Shachi-devi's heart; ānandera nāhi ora — there is no end of joy; o mukha nirakhi — gazing at that face; nāre sambarite — she cannot restrain herself; nayāne bahaye lora — tears flow from her eyes

সীতার চরণে ধরিয়া যতনে কহয়ে মধুর বাণী ।

sītāra caraṇe dhariyā yatane kahaye madhura bāṇī |
kebala bharasā tomādera ogo bhāla manda nāhi jāni ||

আপন জানিয়া নিমাইচাঁদেরে সতত প্রসন্ন হবা ।
চির আয়ু হৈঞা সুখে থাকে যেন এইসে আশীষ দিবা ॥

āpana jāniyā nimāicām̐dere satata prasanna habā |
cira āyu haiñā sukhe thāke yena eise āśīṣa dibā ||

āpana jāniyā — regarding as your own; nimāicām̐dere — to Nimaichand; satata prasanna habā — be always gracious; cira āyu haiñā — living long; sukhe thāke yena — that He may live happily; eise āśīṣa dibā — give this very blessing

কেহ নাহি মোর কত নিবেদিব এ শিশু আঁখির তারা ।
এই করো যেন ঘরে থাকে সদা ঘুচায়ে চঞ্চল ধারা ॥

keha nāhi mora kata nibediba e śiśu ām̐khira tārā |
ei karo yena ghare thāke sadā ghucāye cañcala dhārā ||

keha nāhi mora — I have no one; kata nibediba — what more shall I beg; e śiśu ām̐khira tārā — this child is the pupil of my eye; ei karo — do this; yena ghare thāke sadā — that He always stay at home; ghucāye cañcala dhārā — giving up restless ways

15.4I have no one — what more shall I ask? — this child is the apple of my eye;
make it so that He always stays at home, giving up His restless ways.

আর বলি বিশ্বরূপ মোর এই নিমাই জীবন প্রাণ ।
তিল আধ যেন না হয় বিচ্ছেদ এই বর দিবে দান ॥

āra bali biśvarūpa mora ei nimāi jībana prāṇa |
tila ādha yena nā haya biccheda ei bara dibe dāna ||

āra bali — and I say more; biśvarūpa — Vishvarupa [is gone]; mora ei nimāi — this Nimai of mine; jībana prāṇa — is my life and soul; tila ādha — for half a moment; yena nā haya biccheda — that there be no separation; ei bara dibe dāna — grant this boon

এইরূপ কত কহিয়া তুরিতে করায় মঙ্গল নীত ।

eirūpa kata kahiyā turite karāya maṅgala nīta |

16. Narahari — "śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche…" (GPT1 p. 70, no. 27; GCC)

The elderly women of Navadvipa stand in Shachi's courtyard and gaze at Nimai; each prays for Him: one gives Him all her merit, others will worship Shiva, the Ganga, Chandi, Lakshmi — that He may live long, not leave Nadia, never go abroad to earn money, and be rich; their love for Him is stronger than for their own sons; "may we see this boy in Nadia birth after birth". শচীর আলয় আলো হইয়াছে কি কব সুখের কথা ।
বৃদ্ধানারীগণ মনের হরিষে দাঁড়ায়ে দেখেন তথা ॥

śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche ki kaba sukhera kathā |
bṛddhānārīgaṇa manera hariṣe dām̐ṛāye dekhena tathā ||

śacīra ālaya ālo haiyāche — Shachi's house has become radiant; ki kaba sukhera kathā — what can I say of the happiness; bṛddhā-nārī-gaṇa — the elderly women; manera hariṣe — with joy of heart; dām̐ṛāye dekhena tathā — stand there and gaze

16.1Shachi's house is full of light — what can I say of such happiness!
The elderly women stand there and gaze, rejoicing at heart.

কেহ বলে ওগো কুলের প্রদীপ নিমাই গুণের রাশি ।
আমাদের আঁখি সফল করিতে প্রকট হৈয়াছে আসি ॥

keha bale ogo kulera pradīpa nimāi guṇera rāśi |
āmādera ām̐khi saphala karite prakaṭa haiyāche āsi ||

keha bale — one says; ogo — ah; kulera pradīpa — lamp of the family; nimāi guṇera rāśi — Nimai, a treasury of virtues; āmādera ām̐khi saphala karite — to make our eyes fruitful; prakaṭa haiyāche āsi — has come and appeared

16.2One says: "Ah, the lamp of the family, Nimai, the treasury of virtues,
has come and appeared to make our eyes fruitful."

কেহ বলে ওগো শচীর তনয় সতত কুশলে রহু ।
মোর পুণ্য যত দিলাম ইহারে এড়াউক কণ্টক বহু ॥

keha bale ogo śacīra tanaya satata kuśale rahu |
mora puṇya yata dilāma ihāre eṛāuka kaṇṭaka bahu ||

keha bale — another says; śacīra tanaya — Shachi's son; satata kuśale rahu — may He always be well; mora puṇya yata — all my merit; dilāma ihāre — I have given to Him; eṛāuka kaṇṭaka bahu — may He escape many thorns

16.3Another says: "Ah, may Shachi's son always be well!
I have given Him all my merit — may He escape many thorns."

কেহ বলে ওগো ইহার লাগিয়া পূজিব কৈলাসরাজে ।
চির আয়ু হৈঞা এইরূপে যেন রহয়ে নদীয়া মাঝে ॥

keha bale ogo ihāra lāgiyā pūjiba kailāsarāje |

ihāra lāgiyā — for His sake; pūjiba kailāsa-rāje — I shall worship the Lord of Kailasa; cira āyu haiñā — living long; eirūpe yena rahaye nadīyā mājhe — that He may stay like this in Nadia

কেহ বলে ওগো নিতি নিতি গঙ্গা পূজিয়া মাগিব বর ।

keha bale ogo niti niti gaṅgā pūjiyā māgiba bara |
nijajana laiyā śacīra dulāla ānande karuka ghara ||

niti niti — daily; gaṅgā pūjiyā — worshipping the Ganga; māgiba bara — I shall ask a boon; nija-jana laiyā — with His own people; śacīra dulāla — Shachi's darling; ānande karuka ghara — may He joyfully keep house

caṇḍī pūjiyā — worshipping Chandi; māgiba — I shall ask; manete ye āche mena — what is in my heart; dhana upārjana lāgiyā — to earn money; bideśe nā yāya kakhana yena — that He may never go abroad

কেহ বলে ওগো লক্ষ্মী পূজি আমি আছয়ে কারণ তার ।
অনায়াসে ইহ হবে মহাধনী কভু না ঠেকিবে ভার ॥

keha bale ogo lakṣmī pūji āmi āchaye kāraṇa tāra |
anāyāse iha habe mahādhanī kabhu nā ṭhekibe bhāra ||

lakṣmī pūji āmi — I worship Lakshmi; āchaye kāraṇa tāra — there is a reason for it; anāyāse iha habe mahādhanī — that He may effortlessly become very rich; kabhu nā ṭhekibe bhāra — never will He be hard pressed

16.7Another says: "Ah, I worship Lakshmi, and there is a reason for it:
may He become very rich without effort and never know want."

কেহ বলে ওগো আর শুন কিছু না বুঝি মনের গতি ।
নিজ সুত হৈতে শতগুণ স্নেহ উপজে ইহার প্রতি ॥

keha bale ogo āra śuna kichu nā bujhi manera gati |
nija suta haite śataguṇa sneha upaje ihāra prati ||

āra śuna — listen to this too; kichu nā bujhi manera gati — I do not understand the working of my heart; nija suta haite śata-guṇa sneha — love a hundred times more than for my own son; upaje ihāra prati — arises for Him

কেহ বলে ওগো ঘর তেয়াগিয়া আসিয়া ইহার তরে ।
তিলেক ছাড়িয়া যাইতে না জানি পরাণ কেমন করে ॥

keha bale ogo ghara teyāgiyā āsiyā ihāra tare |
tileka chāṛiyā yāite nā jāni parāṇa kemana kare ||

ghara teyāgiyā — leaving home; āsiyā ihāra tare — I come for His sake; tileka chāṛiyā yāite — to go away even for a moment; nā jāni parāṇa kemana kare — I know not what my soul goes through

কেহ বলে ওগো শচী ভাগ্যবতী অনেক সুকৃতি কৈল ।

keha bale ogo śacī bhāgyabatī aneka sukṛti kaila |
tem̐i sabākāra prāṇadhana ei nadīyācām̐dere pāila ||

śacī bhāgyabatī — fortunate Shachi; aneka sukṛti kaila — performed many pious deeds; tem̐i — therefore; sabākāra prāṇa-dhana — the treasure of life of all; ei nadīyā-cām̐dere pāila — she obtained this Moon of Nadia

কেহ বলে ওগো যে বল সে বল বিধিরে এতেক চাই ।
জনমে জনমে এ বালক যেন নৈদায় দেখিতে পাই ॥

keha bale ogo ye bala se bala bidhire eteka cāi |
janame janame e bālaka yena naidāya dekhite pāi ||

ye bala se bala — say what you will; bidhire eteka cāi — I ask only this of the Creator; janame janame — birth after birth; e bālaka yena naidāya dekhite pāi — that I may see this boy in Nadia

এইরূপে কত প্রেমের আবেশে কহয়ে নাহিক ওর ।
নরহরি কহে এ সবার স্নেহ কহি কি শকতি মোর ॥

eirūpe kata premera ābeśe kahaye nāhika ora |
narahari kahe e sabāra sneha kahi ki śakati mora ||

Narahari says: have I the power to tell of the love of them all?

বৃদ্ধ বৃদ্ধনারী যত অতিশয় আতুর স্নেহের ভরে ।
